First, \(M=0\) is impossible, since then \(\alpha=\beta=0\) would give \(100=0\). Thus \(M>0\).

Write
\[
\alpha=Mz,\qquad \beta=Mw,
\]
where \(|z|=|w|=1\). The given equation becomes
\[
M^2zw+M(z+w)+100=0. \tag{1}
\]

Taking complex conjugates and using \(\bar z=1/z\), \(\bar w=1/w\), we get
\[
M^2\overline{zw}+M(\bar z+\bar w)+100=0,
\]
so
\[
M^2\frac1{zw}+M\left(\frac1z+\frac1w\right)+100=0.
\]
Multiplying by \(zw\),
\[
M^2+M(z+w)+100zw=0. \tag{2}
\]

Subtracting (2) from (1) gives
\[
(M^2-100)(zw-1)=0.
\]

If \(M^2\neq 100\), then \(zw=1\). Substituting \(zw=1\) into (1) gives
\[
M^2+M(z+w)+100=0.
\]
Taking absolute values,
\[
M^2+100=M|z+w|\le 2M.
\]
But for all \(M>0\),
\[
M^2+100-2M=(M-1)^2+99>0,
\]
a contradiction. Therefore we must have \(M^2=100\). Since \(M\ge 0\), this gives \(M=10\).

Finally, \(M=10\) is attainable: take \(\alpha=10\) and \(\beta=-10\). Then
\[
|\alpha|=|\beta|=10
\]
and
\[
\alpha\beta+\alpha+\beta+100=-100+0+100=0.
\]

Thus the only possible value is

\[
\boxed{10}
\]
